annotations.title: Score an MCP server's tool definitions

description:
Score an MCP server's tool definitions for what they ask of the model, before you connect it.
Input: tools, the tools array of a server's tools/list answer (each {name, description, inputSchema}); or server, the server's name as Smithery lists it (for example brave or owner/name), whose published definitions are read from Smithery.
Behavior: runs nothing and calls no server. Fixed rules read each description and every parameter description against the tool's own input schema, because anything in the prose the schema does not need is where an injected instruction lives: tags that frame text as instructions (<IMPORTANT>, <instructions>), HTML comments and invisible characters (zero width, bidirectional controls, Unicode tags), asking the model to drop its instructions, to keep something from the user, or to put a file's contents into an argument, naming files where secrets live (~/.ssh, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.aws), asking for a credential the schema has no parameter for, steering the model off the web or other servers toward this one, and speaking to the model rather than describing the tool. No model reads the text, so the same definitions always get the same findings and anyone can redo them. Keyless, read-only.
Returns: level (clean, review or suspicious), summary, findings (each with tool, rule, severity, where and an excerpt), rulesVersion and inputSha256, the SHA-256 of the definitions as read. A finding is a reason to read the definition, not a verdict on the server: on 500 Smithery servers (12,598 tools, rules 2026-10-31.1) 495 were clean, 3 review and 2 suspicious, and read by hand none hid an order or reached for data: the 3 steer the model off web search toward the server, the 2 were a vendor's response instructions and a false positive.
Not for: what a server's code does when it runs (use kenwea_notary_check on its npm package).

server.description: Alternatively, the server's name as Smithery lists it, for example brave or owner/name.

tools.description: The tools array of the server's tools/list answer.
